issues.problem: 正文把头七周表格中南华克和沃克斯霍尔公司的1,263例死亡和每万户315当作逐户查得的数字来呈现。证据说明，在部分只由该公司供水的分区，怀廷的调查只做到8月5日，后三周的供水是按头四周的比例推算的。

evidence.quote: the water supply of the last three weeks is calculated to have been in the same proportion by the Company, or by pump wells, etc., as in the first four weeks
The sub-districts in which the supply is partly founded on computation, are marked with an asterisk.

issues.proposed: 中英文各加一句：南华克和沃克斯霍尔公司的头七周数字中，部分只由该公司供水的分区后三周按头四周比例推算，并非全部逐户查得（斯诺称这一推算“must be very near the truth”）。

edits.before: 疫情头七周的结果，他整理成一张表。南华克和沃克斯霍尔公司供水40,046户，霍乱死亡1,263人；兰贝斯公司供水26,107户，死亡98人；伦敦其余地区256,423户，死亡1,422人。折算成每10,000户的死亡数，分别是315、37和59。他据此得出结论：南华克和沃克斯霍尔公司供水户的死亡率是兰贝斯公司供水户的八到九倍。但这只是疫情头七周的结果。斯诺自己说明，随着疫情推进，两组的悬殊“没那么大了”，不过仍然十分显著。疫情头四周是每万户71对5，相差十四倍；第二个七周是每万户537对115，接近五倍。截至10月14日的14周里，按每万居民计，南华克和沃克斯霍尔公司供水户死亡153人，兰贝斯公司供水户死亡26人。兰贝斯供水户的死亡率低于全伦敦，但并不低于北区和中区。

edits.before: The first seven weeks of the epidemic went into a single table. Houses supplied by the Southwark and Vauxhall Company: 40,046, with 1,263 deaths from cholera. Lambeth Company: 26,107 houses, 98 deaths. The rest of London: 256,423 houses, 1,422 deaths. Per 10,000 houses that came to 315, 37 and 59. Snow's conclusion: "The mortality in the houses supplied by the Southwark and Vauxhall Company was therefore between eight and nine times as great as in the houses supplied by the Lambeth Company". That was the figure for the first seven weeks only. Snow himself wrote that as the epidemic advanced the disproportion "became not quite so great, although it continued very striking". In the first four weeks it had been 71 against 5 per 10,000 houses, fourteen times. In the second seven weeks it was 537 against 115 per 10,000 houses, nearly five times. Over the 14 weeks ending 14 October, there were 153 deaths per 10,000 living in houses supplied by Southwark and Vauxhall and 26 in houses supplied by Lambeth. The Lambeth figure was lower than London at large, but not lower than the north and central districts.
edits.after: The first seven weeks of the epidemic went into a single table. Houses supplied by the Southwark and Vauxhall Company: 40,046, with 1,263 deaths from cholera. Lambeth Company: 26,107 houses, 98 deaths. The rest of London: 256,423 houses, 1,422 deaths. Per 10,000 houses that came to 315, 37 and 59. Not all of the Southwark and Vauxhall figures for the first seven weeks were checked house by house, though. In some sub-districts supplied only by that company, the inquiry of a medical man, Mr Whiting, extended only to 5 August, and the water supply of the last three weeks was calculated in the same proportion as in the first four weeks; Snow judged that this calculation "must be very near the truth". Snow's conclusion: "The mortality in the houses supplied by the Southwark and Vauxhall Company was therefore between eight and nine times as great as in the houses supplied by the Lambeth Company". That was the figure for the first seven weeks only. Snow himself wrote that as the epidemic advanced the disproportion "became not quite so great, although it continued very striking". In the first four weeks it had been 71 against 5 per 10,000 houses, fourteen times. In the second seven weeks it was 537 against 115 per 10,000 houses, nearly five times. Over the 14 weeks ending 14 October, there were 153 deaths per 10,000 living in houses supplied by Southwark and Vauxhall and 26 in houses supplied by Lambeth. These figures distribute the 795 deaths whose water supply was not ascertained equally over the other sources of supply, and the population of the houses supplied by the two companies is the Registrar General's estimate. The Lambeth figure was lower than London at large, but not lower than the north and central districts.

edits.before: 必须说清楚：本篇所有数字与叙述都出自斯诺本人的书和表格。死者住址来自登记总署。8月26日以后，各区登记员应登记总长的要求，填报了霍乱死亡病例发病房屋的供水情况。这些填报并不完整，仍有一批个案的供水没有查明。斯诺写道，这些填报与他对疫情早期的调查结果“完全一致”。这算是来自登记数据的部分印证，不过我们也只是通过斯诺的书才知道这一点。另外，调查并非全部出自斯诺之手：伯蒙德西等一些只由南华克和沃克斯霍尔公司供水的地区，是由医生约翰·约瑟夫·怀廷（John Joseph Whiting）去调查的。即便如此，学说、统计和呈现它们的这本书都出自斯诺。这不意味着数据有错，但意味着我们读到的是一方的记录。

edits.before: Plainly: every figure and every account in this piece comes from Snow's own book and his own tables. The addresses of the dead came from the General Register Office. After 26 August the district registrars, at the Registrar General's request, returned the water supply of the house of attack in cholera deaths. The returns were incomplete, and the supply "remained unascertained in a number of cases". Even so, Snow says they "agree entirely" with the results of his inquiry into the earlier part of the epidemic. That is partial corroboration from registration data, though it reaches us only through Snow's book. Nor was the whole inquiry Snow's own work. A medical man, John Joseph Whiting, made the inquiries in Bermondsey and certain other districts supplied only by the Southwark and Vauxhall Company. Still, the doctrine, the statistics and the book that presents them are all Snow's. That does not make the data wrong, but it does mean we are reading one side's record.
edits.after: Plainly: every figure and every account in this piece comes from Snow's own book and his own tables. The addresses of the dead came from the General Register Office. After 26 August the district registrars, at the Registrar General's request, returned the water supply of the house of attack in cholera deaths. The returns were incomplete, and the supply "remained unascertained in a number of cases". Even so, Snow says they "agree entirely" with the results of his inquiry into the earlier part of the epidemic. That is partial corroboration from registration data, though it reaches us only through Snow's book. Nor was the whole inquiry Snow's own work. A medical man, John Joseph Whiting, made the inquiries in Bermondsey and certain other districts supplied only by the Southwark and Vauxhall Company. Whiting's part covered only the first four weeks of the epidemic, from 8 July to 5 August, and asked whether each house had the company's water, a pump-well or some other source; in some of these sub-districts the water supply of the last three weeks was calculated in the same proportion as in the first four weeks, not ascertained house by house. Still, the doctrine, the statistics and the book that presents them are all Snow's. That does not make the data wrong, but it does mean we are reading one side's record.

edits.before: 另一种做法（作者设想的替代方案，不是史实）：只比较各区的平均死亡率，或者拿富区和穷区对比。那样贫富、住房、职业都会混进来，水的作用就分不清了。斯诺实际走的是更费事的路：挨家查死者住址、查水，必要时装瓶回家化验。他换来了两样东西。一是同一批混供街道里，按供水分开的死亡户数。二是按两家公司全部供水户计算的每万户死亡比较。

edits.before: Another approach, and this is the author's counterfactual rather than history, would have been to compare average death rates by district, or rich districts against poor ones. Wealth, housing and occupation would then have crowded in, and the effect of the water would have been hard to separate out. What Snow actually did was more laborious: death addresses, house by house, and water carried home in phials. In return he got two things. One was counts of deaths by water supply for houses in the same intermixed streets. The other was a company-wide comparison per 10,000 houses.
edits.after: Another approach, and this is the author's counterfactual rather than history, would have been to compare average death rates by district, or rich districts against poor ones. Wealth, housing and occupation would then have crowded in, and the effect of the water would have been hard to separate out. What Snow actually did was more laborious. He inquired himself into every cholera death in the districts the Lambeth Company supplied: death addresses, house by house, and water carried home in phials. The districts supplied only by the Southwark and Vauxhall Company were covered by a medical man, Mr Whiting, and in some sub-districts the figures for the last three weeks were calculated in proportion. This yielded two things. One was counts of deaths by water supply for houses in the same intermixed streets. The other was a company-wide comparison per 10,000 houses.

He inquired himself into every cholera death in the districts the Lambeth Company supplied: death addresses, house by house, and water carried home in phials.
